knowledge_type_note: A meta-record for the tier where concepts depend on other concepts rather than on board features alone.

history.notes: A meta-record generated from this base's own content; no external history.

preconditions: A concept is being pitched to a reader
recognition.detector: the difficulty field, enforced by tools/schema.json
false_positive_traps: Advanced concepts are the ones this system detects least reliably, because they rest on other concepts rather than on board features. Confidence should be low here even when the reasoning looks clean.
Reaching for an advanced concept because no simple one fits is the standard failure. Saying nothing is better.

limitations: Detection quality falls off sharply in this tier, and the API's confidence ceilings reflect that.

Counts in this record are stated as floors ('over N') rather than exact figures, because the base grows and an exact count written into prose silently becomes false. The live figures are in state/warnings_index.json and state/coverage.json.

NO REGISTERED FALSE-POSITIVE CASE, because this record is about the BASE rather than about boards. It is an index over other concepts, and the conditions it states are conditions on how this system names and files things - not patterns a position can exhibit. A false-positive case here would have to be a mis-filed concept rather than a mistaken reading of a board, and that is what tools/audit.py and tools/validate_kb.py check, on every record, on every run. Recorded rather than filled: tools/depth_report.py still counts this concept as missing the item, and the completion assessment carries the gap.
misconceptions: That advanced concepts are more useful. They are more dependent, which is a different thing and often makes them less usable.

by_level.master: They are also the concepts this system detects worst, and for the same reason.

definition_short: Concepts that rest on other concepts rather than directly on the board — over 30 of them.
definition_long:
The tier where a concept can no longer be explained from the position alone, because it is about the relationship between other ideas.

WHAT PUTS A CONCEPT HERE is a dependency rather than a difficulty. The transformation of an advantage presupposes that you can already identify advantages and know they differ in durability. Prophylaxis presupposes that you can read the opponent's plan. Knight endgames presuppose pawn endgames — that is Botvinnik's formula and it is a dependency stated outright. Piece coordination presupposes piece activity and then says something about the whole army instead of a piece.

THESE ARE ALSO THE CONCEPTS THIS SYSTEM DETECTS WORST, and the two facts are the same fact. A concept that rests on board features can be detected from board features; a concept that rests on other concepts needs those resolved first, and the errors compound. Piece coordination is the clearest case and its own record forbids using it as a fallback label.

DIFFICULTY IN THIS BASE IS ABOUT THE CONCEPT, NOT THE PLAYER. It records how much other machinery a concept needs before it can be stated truthfully, which is why some famous ideas sit high and some obscure ones sit low. A fork is a beginner concept because it can be stated completely in one sentence; the Vancura position is an expert one not because it is hard to play but because stating it correctly requires the rook-ending context in which Tarrasch's rule fails.

IT IS ALSO WHAT DRIVES LEVEL ADAPTATION. Every concept carries explanations.by_level with wording for beginner, intermediate, advanced and master, and the API selects among them. The difficulty field says where a concept BELONGS; the by_level wording says how to say it to whoever is asking. The two are deliberately separate, because an advanced concept still has to be explicable to a beginner who has just met it on the board.
